grounding.proposition: PASS=0 and FAIL=1 are explicit DMR reporting codes entered in the CONCENTRATION MAX field, not numeric pollutant concentrations.
Pass/fail parameters use LIMIT_UNIT_DESC=pass=0;fail=1 with empty LIMIT_VALUE_NMBR, so no numeric effluent limit is paired for ordinary concentration comparison.
Report 1 when NOEC for survival is less than the critical dilution (fail); otherwise report 0 (pass).
Numeric NOEC concentration is reported separately on TOM3D/TOM6C parameters, not via the 0/1 pass/fail code.
Observed reporting uses categorical 0 with pass=0;fail=1 units and no paired numeric limit value.

interpretation: PASS=0 and FAIL=1 are categorical whole-effluent-toxicity DMR outcome codes: 0 means the test passed (NOEC for survival is not less than the critical dilution) and 1 means the test failed (NOEC for survival is less than the critical dilution). They are not ordinary numeric pollutant concentrations to compare against a concentration-based effluent limit; numeric NOEC values, when required, are reported on separate TOM parameters in percent.
remaining_uncertainty: The numeric value of critical dilution is not encoded as LIMIT_VALUE_NMBR on pass/fail rows, so automated pass/fail determination from structured fields alone is incomplete. Retest STORET codes share the same semantics but are optional and may not apply unless a retest was triggered. Evidence is limited to permit NM0020583 (Farmington) and its 12 WET limit rows.
